item.title: Early-Life Sugar Rationing Reduced Heart Failure Risk
item.description: Those exposed to early-life sugar rationing had an approximately 14% lower risk of developing heart failure and were diagnosed an average of 2.6 years later than individuals who were unexposed. The post Early-Life Sugar Rationing Reduced Heart Failure Risk appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Bimekizumab Shows Durable Long-Term Psoriasis Clearance
item.description: Researchers identified a distinct population of tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells expressing IL-17A and/or IL-17F that were largely absent from healthy skin. The post Bimekizumab Shows Durable Long-Term Psoriasis Clearance appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Major Depressive Disorder Linked to Poorer Asthma Control
item.description: Major depressive disorder predicted long-term asthma outcomes in adults 60+ with beliefs mediating control QoL, and steroid bursts. The post Major Depressive Disorder Linked to Poorer Asthma Control appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: New Global Strategy Targets Gaps in Fertility Care Access
item.description: A new global strategy calls for infertility care to be integrated into reproductive health systems to improve access and equity worldwide. The post New Global Strategy Targets Gaps in Fertility Care Access appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Repeat Influenza Vaccination May Blunt Early Immunity
item.description: How does repeat influenza vaccination affect antibody responses? Study finds early immune boosts may be smaller, but protection later remains similar. The post Repeat Influenza Vaccination May Blunt Early Immunity appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Hajj Travel: Meningitis Vaccine Performs Well for Older Pilgrims
item.description: A meningitis vaccine generated bactericidal antibodies in Hajj/Umrah travelers, with solid postvaccination safety through 30 days. The post Hajj Travel: Meningitis Vaccine Performs Well for Older Pilgrims appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Human Parvovirus B19 Drives Bone Marrow Failure
item.description: Parvovirus B19 was shown to infect haematopoietic stem cells, impairing self renewal and differentiation, with JAK2 STAT5 inhibition partially reversing virus induced bone marrow dysfunction. The post Human Parvovirus B19 Drives Bone Marrow Failure appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Sex Differences in Alzheimer’s Disease Biomarkers at Age 60
item.description: New imaging data reveal striking sex differences in Alzheimer’s disease biomarkers, with implications for diagnosis and personalised dementia care. The post Sex Differences in Alzheimer’s Disease Biomarkers at Age 60 appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Artificial Urinary Sphincter Demonstrates Strong Efficacy and Safety
item.description: A multicentre prospective trial shows the artificial urinary sphincter delivers high continence rates, improved quality of life, and a low revision rate in men. The post Artificial Urinary Sphincter Demonstrates Strong Efficacy and Safety appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Scientists Rethink the Biological Drivers of Severe Asthma
item.description: Mean urinary concentrations of two pseudo leukotrienes were elevated four- to five-fold in individuals with severe asthma compared with controls (P=0.004 and P=0.0015). The post Scientists Rethink the Biological Drivers of Severe Asthma appeared first on European Medical Journal.
